statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-69304 (GHSA-8cp2-47hg-mfgh) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in the IIS integration middleware used for IIS out-of-process hosting: it did not properly constrain decompression of certain requests, leading to excess memory use. Microsoft lists Windows with IIS out-of-process hosting as the affected platform and the Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IISIntegration package as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.30 and fixed in 8.0.31 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8cp2-47hg-mfgh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/443, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.31/8.0.31.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold. The native IIS module (ASP.NET Core Module) is not in any of the packages, but Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IISIntegration.dll is part of the cross-platform Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework, so the middleware code is present: implementation copies are in the shared framework in aspnetcore8-runtime and in the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and each carries the build's own .NET version: 8.0.23 to 8.0.29 in the first six builds and 8.0.31 or later from 8.0.31-r0 on. The other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. Because the code ships and the fix ships with it, this owner is recorded as fixed rather than not affected. The range ends at 8.0.31-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-69304 (GHSA-8cp2-47hg-mfgh) is an ASP.NET Core denial of service issue in IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression: the IIS middleware did not properly constrain decompression of certain requests, which can exhaust memory. Microsoft lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IISIntegration as affected from 9.0.0 through 9.0.19 and fixed in 9.0.20, with Windows and IIS out-of-process hosting as the affected platform (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8cp2-47hg-mfgh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/443, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.20/9.0.20.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. No 9.0.19 build was published; the build after 9.0.18-r0 is 9.0.20-r0. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.IISIntegration.dll is part of the cross-platform Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework, so implementation copies are in aspnetcore9-runtime, in the .NET SDK held by dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap and in the ASP.NET Core runtime pack in dotnet9-runtime-bootstrap; the other copies are reference assemblies with no implementation code. Every implementation copy carries the build's own .NET version: 9.0.12 to 9.0.18 in the first seven builds and 9.0.20 or later from 9.0.20-r0 on. The IIS native module that forwards requests to the application is a Windows component and is not in these packages, but the affected middleware code ships, so this is recorded as fixed rather than not affected. The range ends at 9.0.20-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
